See /kobuki_node/src/node/diagnostics.cpp" and commit bb3c7ec "Fix issue #136: Battery charge not shown in Android apps". The consuming code (TurtlebotDashboard.java in the Turtlebot Android app library) is public and shows exactly the name and keys the fix introduces.

E2.evidence: Unit 1: kobuki_node (run as node "mobile_base" by kobuki_bringup/minimal.launch), whose BatteryTask publishes a diagnostic_msgs status named "Battery" (prefixed by the node name by diagnostic_updater) with key-values "Capacity", "Voltage", "Percent", "Source", "State"; the same bringup launches diagnostic_aggregator with kobuki_bringup's diagnostics.yaml, which re-publishes it on /diagnostics_agg under path 'Power System'. Unit 2: the Turtlebot Android apps' dashboard (ros.android.views.TurtlebotDashboard in android_app_manager), a separate rosjava process that subscribes to diagnostics_agg, selects the status whose name equals "/Power System/Battery" and reads the keys "Charge (Ah)", "Capacity (Ah)" and "Current (A)". Step 2: the failure is entirely about values crossing the boundary (the status name string and the key strings of the DiagnosticStatus payload), not a defect internal to either unit. Step 3: the minimal fix is not only name binding: besides the aggregator's remove_prefix configuration it changes the provider's published key-values in kobuki_node/src/node/diagnostics.cpp. Step 4/5: not build or firmware. Interface kind: topic (diagnostic_msgs/DiagnosticArray content on /diagnostics_agg).

E3.evidence: PAIR: the battery diagnostic published by kobuki_node (through the aggregator) feeds the dashboard's diagnostics_agg subscriber; both units run together and nothing was upgraded or switched.

E4.evidence: Observed failure named in the issue title and commit message: "Battery charge not shown in Android apps"; the consumer code documents the silent no-data path: `catch (NullPointerException ex) { // Do nothing: data wasn't there. }` after `values.get("Charge (Ah)")` / `values.get("Capacity (Ah)")`.

failed_conditions.quote: I modified diagnostics.yaml to remove the node name (by adding remove_prefix: mobile_base)

loudness_evidence: No diagnostic from any tooling: the dashboard's battery view simply stayed empty ("Battery charge not shown in Android apps", https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki/issues/136). The consumer swallows the missing keys: `} catch (NullPointerException ex) { // Do nothing: data wasn't there. }` (https://github.com/ros-android/android_app_manager/blob/f080cd934460fc92babd48eee5f660454c1b48d0/library/src/ros/android/views/TurtlebotDashboard.java).

resolution.summary: Commit bb3c7ec, two changes on the kobuki side: (1) kobuki_bringup/resources/yaml/diagnostics.yaml adds `remove_prefix: mobile_base` to each GenericAnalyzer so the aggregated status is named "/Power System/Battery" instead of carrying the "mobile_base: " node-name prefix; (2) kobuki_node/src/node/diagnostics.cpp BatteryTask::run() publishes the key-values the dashboard reads, "Charge (Ah)" (capacity times percent / 100), "Capacity (Ah)" (2.2), "Current (A)" (3.14 when Charged/Charging, 0.0 when Discharging), and renames "Voltage" to "Voltage (V)". The Android app is unchanged.
resolution.evidence: Maintainer corot closing the issue: "Fixed with two changes: - I modified diagnostics.yaml to remove the node name (by adding remove_prefix: mobile_base) - We send Current Charge and Capacity diagnostic values." (https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki/issues/136#issuecomment-6444016). No log or screenshot is posted; the app revision of the resolved composition is the inferred f080cd9 (unchanged).

notes: Both conditions are naming conventions of strings inside the diagnostic_msgs payload rather than ROS interface elements, hence class other. Condition 1 (status name): diagnostic_updater names the status "<node name>: <task name>" (node "mobile_base", BatteryTask("Battery")); GenericAnalyzer with `contains: ['Battery', 'Laptop Battery']` and path 'Power System' emitted "/Power System/mobile_base: Battery" until remove_prefix stripped the prefix; the consumer tests `status.name.equals("/Power System/Battery")`. Condition 2 (key names/encoding): the provider encoded the level as "Percent"/"Voltage"/"Capacity" while the consumer computes `100 * Float.parseFloat(values.get("Charge (Ah)")) / Float.parseFloat(values.get("Capacity (Ah)"))` and `view.setPluggedIn( Float.parseFloat(values.get("Current (A)")) > 0)`; corot's notes explain the hard-coded 3.14 A / 2.2 Ah values chosen to satisfy that computation. The topic hop: kobuki_node publishes /diagnostics; diagnostic_aggregator (diagnostics stack, launched and configured by kobuki_bringup) publishes /diagnostics_agg, which the dashboard subscribes to as "diagnostics_agg"; the aggregator is treated as part of the provider's deployment, not as a third unit, because its configuration lives in the kobuki repository and only forwards kobuki_node's content. The aggregator part of the fix alone would be deployment configuration; the case is eligible because the key-value change is a code change to the provider's published content. The laptop battery status (kobuki_node/scripts laptop_battery.py, "/Power System/Laptop Battery") is a separate composition not discussed in the source.
